items.summary: CRO disposition: reject both candidate product proposals this cycle. The work-admission control plane is relevant because the fleet has 10/10 active slots, 105 approved proposals without execution requests, 21 failed requests, and 39 deployed improvements awaiting measurement; however, implementation would add capacity and queue work before the canonical saveusfarms.com repair is closed. The measurement-debt cockpit is also relevant because 39 improvements await measurement and only 6 are proven, but it should remain a deferred read-only product hypothesis. No CRO proposal is retained. Preserve the smallest future prototypes as planning notes: a read-only duplicate/admission report using existing records, and a read-only measurement-outcome table. Success metrics would be fewer duplicate admissions, higher proposal execution rate, and more deployed improvements reaching a disposition; time-to-learn is one operating cycle after capacity clears. No telemetry, deployment, spend, credentials, or production changes are requested.

CRO handoff: no new implementation or research admission is recommended while delivery remains saturated at 10/10 slots. The strongest deferred product opportunity is a read-only fleet work-admission/deduplication prototype over existing proposal, request, work-item, active-slot, overlap, failure, and measurement records. Smallest reversible prototype: generate one report identifying duplicate identities, blocked admissions, missing execution links, and the single next owner action; do not modify queue behavior. A second deferred prototype is a read-only measurement-debt table showing baseline availability, due date, attribution limits, and terminal outcome state. Validate usefulness by reduced no-action cycles and faster disposition recording after capacity clears. Existing security, legal, attribution, and measurement gates remain unchanged.
